purpose: Single source of truth for Sidecar setup. The onboarding wizard renders this as a form; INTERVIEW.md covers the same fields conversationally. Both write the same files. If you add a {{PLACEHOLDER}} anywhere in LOOP_PROMPT.md, JOURNAL.md, or ops/, add its field here.

conventions.maps_to: Template placeholders this field fills. One field may fill several files.
conventions.derived: Computed from other fields or the environment — never asked of the user.
conventions.delete_if_empty: Sections that must be removed outright (heading and all) when the field is empty — a cold agent will try to satisfy a stub.
conventions.default_marker: Defaults are written into output files with this suffix so the user knows to confirm them.

rounds.title: Frame it
rounds.intro: This runs an AI agent against a real brokerage account on a schedule. Once live, it places real orders without asking first, on days you've forgotten about it. That's the design; everything below makes sure it happens inside limits you actually chose.

options.label: Live
options.description: Real orders from the first trade. Robinhood has no paper environment.

options.label: Paper
options.description: Only if your broker offers a paper endpoint (e.g. Alpaca).

fields.label: What would make you shut it off?
fields.help: Worth more than any risk questionnaire. 'If it lost half', 'if it bought meme stocks', 'if it traded every day' — whatever you'd actually say. Becomes a hard constraint.

rounds.title: The account
rounds.intro: Grab your phone for this one. In the Robinhood app: enable agent trading, complete your investment profile (buys block until you do), and find your account number under the account icon, then the menu, then Settings. Robinhood designates ONE account for agent trading when you enable it; use that account's number below.

options.label: Robinhood
options.description: Reference path. Agent trading enabled in the app; one designated account.

options.label: Alpaca
options.description: Has paper + live endpoints.

options.label: Other
options.description: Any broker with an MCP server or API covering quotes, positions, orders.

fields.label: MCP server name
fields.note: Auto-filled from broker; editable for 'other'. Tool names are unprefixed on Robinhood.

fields.label: Robinhood account number
fields.help: Every read and order carries this, and Robinhood designates ONE specific account for agent trading when you enable it, so use that one. Find it in the app: account icon (bottom right), then the menu, then Settings, where the account number is listed. Stuck? Finish setup anyway, connect the Robinhood connector on claude.ai, and ask Claude to 'call get_accounts': the answer is the exact identifier, and your agent can amend LOOP_PROMPT.md with it.

options.label: Taxable
options.description: Short-term gains and wash-sale exposure apply.

options.label: Tax-advantaged (IRA etc.)
options.description: No wash-sale or short-term-gain concerns inside the account.

fields.label: Starting capital
fields.help: Rough is fine. The loop reads live buying power every cycle regardless.

options.label: Crypto
options.description: Note: Robinhood's agent server has no crypto tools — allowed strategically, unavailable operationally.

fields.label: Options approval level
fields.note: Rendered empty (omitted) when options are not in instruments.

fields.label: Is there a portfolio outside this account?

options.value: satellite sleeve alongside an existing core portfolio
options.label: Yes — this is a sidecar
options.description: The sleeve earns its existence by expressing what the core can't: single names, themes, tactical trades.

options.value: intended to become the core portfolio
options.label: No — this is the core
options.description: Tilts the mandate toward diversification and boring quality.

fields.label: Rough shape of the outside portfolio
fields.help: 'Mostly index funds, a 401k' is enough. No figures needed.

show_if.sleeve_role: satellite sleeve alongside an existing core portfolio

fields.label: What should the loop NOT duplicate?
fields.help: If your core is an S&P index fund, the sleeve gains nothing buying SPY. List exposures the core already holds.
fields.default: broad index ETFs already held in the core portfolio

show_if.sleeve_role: satellite sleeve alongside an existing core portfolio

fields.label: Want a per-cycle one-line read on accounts this loop can't trade?
fields.help: Advice only, costs one line. Name the accounts and holdings.

fields.label: What do you actually believe about markets?
fields.help: Pick the closest and edit. An agent with no stated edge buys whatever was in the news that morning.
presets: Buy quality companies at fair prices and hold — edge is patience, not information. Will not chase momentum or rotate on headlines.
Find stories the market hasn't priced yet — edge is being early to a thesis. Will not average down into a broken one.
Catch mispricings and rotate — edge is speed of recognition. Will not hold losers hoping.
Ride momentum with strict exits — edge is discipline, not prediction. Will not hold through a broken trend.

fields.label: A thesis you already hold (optional)
fields.help: In your words, with the why. Most people setting this up have one.
fields.default: no fixed opening thesis — scan broadly and let the entry test find the first positions

fields.label: What would change your mind about it?
fields.help: Something falsifiable. 'If revenue growth drops below X' beats 'if things look bad'. Becomes the break test the loop runs every cycle.
fields.default: a holding's stated reason to own it stops being true — not a price move alone, but the thesis itself

fields.label: Should it deliberately look outside your thesis every cycle?
fields.help: Strongly recommended. Concentrated books drift into monocultures.

options.value: Every cycle, scan at least three sectors outside the current thesis. A name outside the thesis that passes the entry test gets a starter position — no exceptions.
options.label: Yes, with teeth (recommended)
options.description: An outside name that passes the entry test is a mandatory starter position.

options.value: Every cycle, scan sectors outside the thesis and journal what was found and why it was passed or acted on.
options.label: Yes, advisory
options.description: Must look and journal, but not obligated to act.

options.label: No
options.description: Higher monoculture risk. The section is deleted from the mandate if you pick this.

fields.label: How will you know it's working?

options.value: total return vs. the same dollars in an S&P 500 index fund, re-evaluated quarterly
options.label: Beat an S&P 500 index fund

options.value: total return vs. the same dollars in a Nasdaq-100 index fund, re-evaluated quarterly
options.label: Beat a Nasdaq-100 index fund

options.value: learning and process quality — re-evaluate on journal review, not returns
options.label: I'm doing this to learn

fields.label: Max size of any single position
Most any single name may grow to
fields.help: Trimming back past the ceiling is how a good call is kept from quietly becoming the whole book.

options.value: forbidden — no leveraged ETFs, no 0DTE, no decay products
options.label: Forbidden (recommended)

options.value: allowed only with an explicit stop, a time-box, and a journaled thesis on every entry
options.label: Allowed with strict rules

fields.label: Never allowed
fields.help: Shorting, penny stocks, sectors you won't own — plus whatever you said would make you shut it off.

fields.label: If the sleeve is down 25%, the loop should…
fields.help: Decide now, while nobody is losing money.

options.value: down 25% from peak: stop opening new positions, journal a full review, manage existing only
options.label: Stop opening, review (recommended)

options.value: down 25% from peak: de-risk to at least 50% cash and journal a full review
options.label: De-risk to cash

options.value: down 25% from peak: no automatic action — drawdowns are expected; re-examine the thesis, not the balance
options.label: Nothing automatic

fields.label: How much autonomy?
fields.help: The consequential setting. Propose-only is a genuinely good way to spend the first few weeks.

options.value: PROPOSE-ONLY — place NO orders. State the exact order you would place, journal it, leave it for the owner.
options.label: Propose-only (recommended to start)
options.description: Full analysis and journaling; orders wait for you.

derives.AUTONOMY_LINE: PROPOSE-ONLY — place NO orders. State the exact order you would place, journal it, leave it for the owner.

options.value: FULL AUTONOMY — no user confirmation needed for any trade.
options.label: Full autonomy
options.description: Places orders unattended. Can lose money while you sleep.

derives.AUTONOMY_LINE: FULL AUTONOMY — no user confirmation needed for any trade.

options.value: MIXED — autonomous up to a per-order threshold; above it, propose only.
options.label: Mixed
options.description: Autonomous under a threshold, approval above it.

fields.label: Per-order threshold ($)

show_if.autonomy: MIXED — autonomous up to a per-order threshold; above it, propose only.

fields.note: MIXED renders AUTONOMY_LINE as 'Place orders up to $THRESHOLD without confirmation; above that, journal the proposed order and leave it.'

options.label: 3× per weekday
options.description: Reference cadence.

options.label: Weekly
options.description: Legitimate for a long-horizon mandate.

options.label: Cloud (recommended)
options.description: Nothing on your machine; laptop can be shut. The wizard drives this path.

options.label: Local
options.description: Fully under your control; stops when the laptop sleeps.

fields.label: Anything extra every journal entry should include?
What's the one rule you'd be upset if this thing broke?
fields.help: A stock you'd never sell, a date you need cash by, a hard ceiling on what's at risk.

derived_fields.rule: the GitHub repo created during setup
local: absolute clone path; cloud: the repo root in the runner checkout
from broker option's derives, or free text for 'other'
from autonomy option's derives; MIXED renders with autonomy_threshold
wizard default: a frontier model (currently 'opus' for the local path)
local scheduler only: `which claude` at setup time
local scheduler only: `which node` at setup time

outputs.PROFILE.md: All answers by round, in the user's words, with reasoning; defaults marked per conventions.default_marker.
outputs.LOOP_PROMPT.md: Every placeholder filled; declined sections deleted outright per delete_if_empty; operational sections never deleted.
outputs.JOURNAL.md: Standing rules from hard limits + CYCLE 0 entry.
outputs.ops/run.sh: Filled even for cloud-only users — it's the fallback. CLI_PATH/NODE_PATH only when local.
outputs.routine_handoff: ops/ROUTINE_PROMPT.md rendered with the user's values as one copy-pasteable block, plus the config checklist (tools allowlist including Bash, connector, model, cron with DST caveat, persist_session off).
